1.why: Density measures mass per unit volume of substances like smoke and air.

wrong.a: Volume is measured in cubic metres.

2.why: Mass divided by volume gives the density value in kg per cubic metre.

wrong.b: Multiplying mass and volume is incorrect.
wrong.c: Volume divided by mass is reciprocal density.
wrong.d: Subtracting volume from mass is invalid.

3.why: Fires release dense smoke particles into the air across the region [1].

_quiz_pool.question: What does rho (ρ) represent in the density equation?
_quiz_pool.explanation: Rho stands for density in kg/m³.

_quiz_pool.question: Which unit is used for density in physics?
_quiz_pool.explanation: Density is measured in kilograms per cubic metre.

_quiz_pool.question: If mass increases while volume stays constant, density will...
_quiz_pool.explanation: More mass in the same volume increases density.

_quiz_pool.question: What does V stand for in density calculation?
_quiz_pool.explanation: V represents volume in cubic metres.

_quiz_pool.question: What do hotspots detected by satellites represent?
_quiz_pool.explanation: Hotspots show high radiant heat from fires or land clearing.

_quiz_pool.question: What does m stand for in physics equations?
_quiz_pool.explanation: m stands for mass in kilograms.

safety: no open flames or mains electricity
_lab_rubric.pass_if: Students show understanding of density differences between materials.

story.title: Fires and corporate concessions
story.lead: Thousands of hotspots have been recorded across Indonesia, with many located inside corporate palm oil and timber concessions [1]. Weather agencies track these events during dry transitions [2].

story.body_1: Forest and land fires create severe ecological pressure and release dense smoke into the atmosphere [1]. Satellite monitoring systems detect these anomalies as hotspots [1].
story.body_2: Understanding the density of smoke particles helps scientists evaluate air quality and environmental impact [2]. Proper governance and enforcement remain crucial for prevention [1].
timeline.1.text: Hotspot monitoring begins across Indonesian provinces [1].
timeline.2.text: Tens of thousands of hotspots are tallied by satellite sensors [1].
physics.title: Density calculation
physics.body_1: When materials burn, they release smoke and ash with specific mass and volume. Density tells us how tightly packed the matter is within a given space.
physics.body_2: Density rho equals mass divided by volume. Denser smoke particles stay suspended or settle slowly depending on atmospheric conditions.
physics.assumptions: Assumes uniform composition and constant volume during particle dispersion.
